_notes.design: The model never writes to the vault. It returns a typed plan (merge_facts, supersede, rewrite_index, compact_sessions) and this script validates and applies each operation mechanically. That is what makes an unattended memory rewrite auditable and revertible.
_notes.safety: A file is eligible only if it is TRACKED and CLEAN in git. Untracked files are not recoverable if a merge goes wrong, and dirty files belong to one of the 10-30 concurrent sessions writing this vault. Both are skipped and reported, never rewritten.
_notes.sessions: Compaction digests per project per month, and deletes the originals ONLY because all 848 are git-tracked, so history remains the audit trail. Verified 2026-08-06: 0 of 848 untracked.
_notes.never_delete: A fact file is never deleted. A merged one is replaced by a tombstone pointing at the canonical file, so every old link still resolves.
_notes.sweepCostCapUsd: Hard ceiling per run. Pilot measured $0.38-0.53 per project. With change-detection most runs touch only the 1-3 projects that actually moved, so a typical run is well under $1; the cap bounds the worst case at 4 runs/day to about $16/day.
_notes.cadence: Every 6h via launchd. node is the entrypoint because TCC grants are per-binary: /bin/zsh is denied ~/Documents under launchd, node at its absolute path is granted. Verified by probe 2026-08-06.
_notes.forceAfterHours: A project unchanged since its last sweep is skipped and costs nothing. This forces a pass anyway after 168h (7 days) so a stale index cannot hide behind unchanged forever.
_notes.mergeCompressionFloor: A merged body must keep at least 40% of the combined bytes of its sources. The first live run cut 8733B to 1287B (15%) while claiming no facts were lost, having dropped Composer from the flat-rate routing rule. Deduplication removes repetition, not content.
_notes.strayDrain: Scheduled drain of unwrapped transcripts. /wrap only mines 8 per run because it reads each into the live session's context, so the backlog outran it and sessions began declining the work. maxPerRun bounds one run; the job is restartable and the ledger prevents double-mining. Summarisation routes to the cheap open-weight tier at roughly $0.004 per transcript; transcripts the privacy gate refuses are re-run with --engine claude so they bill the subscription and never leave the machine.
_notes.plannerFailover: Typed memory plans use the Claude subscription first, then the ChatGPT subscription through Codex when quota, plan-limit, credential, timeout, circuit, unavailable-provider, or malformed-response failures occur. Policy, privacy, input, and authorization failures hard-stop. Both children receive no metered API keys; Codex is ephemeral and read-only.
